newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Patten lobbies Japan on post-1997 visas.
newsitem.headline: HK's Patten lobbies Japan on post-1997 visas.

text.p: Hong Kong Governor Chris Patten said on Tuesday he would press Japan to grant Hong Kong people visa-free entry after the British colony reverts to Chinese sovereignty next year.

Speaking to reporters before leaving for Tokyo where he will meet Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto, Patten said he would try to persuade Japan to afford Hong Kong's post-1997 passports preferential treatment over mainland Chinese passports.

"The principle task while I am in Japan will be to encourage the Japanese to ensure the Special Administrative Region passports are treated differently from and more favourably than People's Republic of China passports," he said.
Patten will spend five days in Japan.
More than 150 years of British colonial rule will end at midnight next June 30 when Hong Kong reverts to China as a Special Administrative Region (SAR).
So far only Britain, Singapore and Western Samoa have promised SAR passport holders visa-free entry.
